title: Exploited Chrome V8 type confusion can execute code inside the browser sandbox
summary: Google fixed CVE-2026-85046 in its September 3 security update and confirmed an exploit in the wild. A crafted HTML page can execute code inside the sandbox through V8 type confusion. This is a historical flaw identified during the current lead review, not a new November disclosure.

severity.rationale: Crafted web content reaches code execution, and Google confirms exploitation in the wild. Confirmed exploitation reaching code execution warrants a 24-hour response under this rubric; the CVE establishes execution inside the sandbox, not a standalone sandbox escape.

exploitation.note: Google confirms an exploit exists in the wild in its September 3, 2026 release notice. The CVE record includes CISA KEV metadata with a date added of 2026-09-04.

affected.note: Google lists 152.0.7977.82/.83 for Windows and macOS and 152.0.7977.82 for Linux.

exposure: Affected Chrome instances processing untrusted HTML are exposed, including agent-driven browsing. The primary description limits this flaw alone to execution inside the sandbox.

remediation.details: Install a current patched Chrome release at or above 152.0.7977.82 and restart browser processes. This historical floor addresses this CVE only.
remediation.risk: Low. Restarting interrupts active browsing sessions.

verification: Confirm the running browser executable reports the patched version after restart.

discovery.note: Generic Chrome 12-fix lead prompted a primary-source check. The verified September advisory is recorded with its historical date; the post does not identify this CVE.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review from the historical September vendor notice.
Added the CISA KEV listing and September 4, 2026 inclusion date from CISA enrichment in the CVE record.
